title: Goonzquad's rat-chewed, rear-ended 2026 Corvette ZR1 turns into its biggest rebuild yet
dek: A 2,100-mile, 1,064-hp ZR1 bought on a salvage title has eaten more than $30,000 in parts plus an $18,000 replacement transmission, and it still hasn't run.

source.where: An auction yard; house and location not named in the coverage
source.boughtNote: Not disclosed. The brothers said they paid "about 50% off" (autoevolution), but gave no figure.

source.damage: Heavy rear impact: three wheels missing, rear bumper, exhaust and crash bar gone or hanging, rear subframe, rear tub and both rear frame rails broken, shock pushed through its mount, cracked transmission case with a damaged gear, axle pulled out; rodent damage to seats, console, dash and wiring. Front end and engine appear sound.

value.basis: Clean C8 ZR1s on Bring a Trailer sold for $223,000 (cheapest 2026 coupe) to $301,000 (2025 Launch Edition convertible), and classic.com's average of eight resales was $273,375; a rebuilt/salvage title typically takes 20% to 40% off, giving roughly $135,000 to $215,000 for this car once finished.

verdict: Still too early to call, and the margin is thinning. With the purchase price unstated, the parts bill is now at least $48,000 once the $18,000 replacement transmission is added, before the rat-chewed body harness and interior are priced. A rebuilt-title ZR1 should still be worth well into six figures, so a profit is possible only if the brothers really paid around half of a $220,000-plus sticker. The bigger lesson is the gearbox: GM's refusal to sell the internals turned a repair into an $18,000 swap, against roughly $5,000 for an ordinary used C8 transmission, which is how parts policy, not damage, sets the price of a rebuild.
body:
## The buy

Goonzquad, the Tennessee brothers Eleazar and Simeon who rebuild wrecked cars, opened the project on September 12, 2026 with "We Bought a DESTROYED C8 Corvette ZR1!" [1]. The car is a 2026 C8 Corvette ZR1, the 1,064-hp twin-turbo flagship, in Arctic White with racing stripes, a Habanero interior, carbon roof and black Carbon Flash forged wheels, with about 2,100 miles on the cluster [1][2]. Reporting says it was one of the first wrecked C8 ZR1s to reach auction [3].

It came from an auction yard on a salvage title [2]. Neither the video coverage nor the reporting names the auction house or location, and the purchase price was not disclosed. The brothers said they got it for "about 50% off" [2], and autoevolution put the original sticker of this well-optioned car at well over $220,000 against a $197,700 base price [2]. Half of that would be somewhere north of $100,000, but that is arithmetic on a remark, not a stated figure, so this file leaves the price paid blank.

## The damage

The crash came from behind. The car arrived missing three of its four wheels and sitting on its belly, with part of the rear end, the rear bumper and much of the exhaust gone [2]. The rear crash bar was pushed down and hanging, the rear subframe was deformed, the driver-side quarter panel was cracked open far enough to expose the ECU, and wiring was dangling [2]. Hairline cracks showed in the transmission mounting area [2][3]. The good news: the front end and most of the carbon-fiber pieces survived, and the floor and underbody were largely intact, with the serious damage concentrated from the firewall rearward [3][4].

Then there was the rat. A rodent had nested in the car and chewed the center console, dashboard leather, door trim, the carbon-fiber bucket seats, a hose and some wiring [2][3]. The electrical system was dead, so the door had to be opened with an emergency latch tool [2].

Teardown made it worse. In the second episode, "We Tore Apart Our Wrecked C8 ZR1… It's Worse Than We Thought" (September 16), the fiberglass rear tub turned out to be destroyed, a rear shock had been pushed through its mount, and both rear frame rails were broken, the passenger side worst [5]. The crack near the transmission had become a broken-off end section, and an axle shaft had been pulled out of the transmission at an angle, with signs of bearing damage and a gear with damaged splines and missing teeth [5]. The one big relief: the crankshaft turned, so the 1,064-hp engine did not appear seized, and the brothers decided to carry on [5].

## The work and the parts

By the end of the first video the brothers had already ordered about $23,000 in parts from dealers, eBay and GM's parts site: a wiring harness, left rear suspension, an axle shaft, doors, quarter panels and rocker panels, with a rear tub and frame rails possibly to follow [2][4]. Some pieces are shared with the C8 Z06, but ZR1-only parts have to come from Chevrolet [3]. They weighed dealer seats but noted those alone would roughly double the cost of the project, so the plan is to save original parts where they can [2].

The second episode added two rear frame rails to the list. Their part numbers suggest they are shared with non-convertible C8s, which leaves a donor car as a fallback [5]. The transmission, which carries ZR1-specific internals, has to come off the engine and be opened up, and the engine harness will probably need replacing [5].

In the third episode, "Our Wrecked Corvette ZR1 Rebuild Just Got EXPENSIVE!" (October 9), the channel says they uncovered serious transmission damage, installed new frame rails and unboxed more than $30,000 worth of parts [6]. In about four weeks and three episodes the car had gone from teardown to new rear structure, but it was not yet running.

The fourth episode, "We Finally Put Our Destroyed C8 ZR1 Back Together!" (October 31), settled the gearbox question the expensive way [11]. The brothers bought a replacement transmission for $18,000 because, as one put it, GM "really didn't want to provide us with the parts" to repair the original [10]. They took the old unit apart and compared it with other C8 transmissions, suspecting the ZR1 version has strengthened input shafts, but could not find enough differences to explain the price; an ordinary used C8 transmission, one brother noted, runs about $5,000 [10]. The new transmission went onto a replacement subframe and the assembly was lowered into the car. The rear fiberglass structure was bonded to the new frame, and the quarter panels, rear bumper, trunk lid and wing were test-fitted; one brother said the parts "lined up really, really good" [10]. The rat damage kept growing, though: more chewed wiring turned up, including a body harness tied to the car's electronic systems, which may mean pulling the dashboard and much of the interior [10].

## The money

What is on the record: about $23,000 in parts ordered by episode one [2], "over $30,000" in parts unboxed in episode three [6], and an $18,000 transmission in episode four [10]. It is not clear whether the second figure includes the first, so this file counts $30,000 as a floor and adds the transmission, which was still being diagnosed when the $30,000 was unboxed: at least $48,000 in parts. The purchase price is unknown, and the body harness, interior work and any specialist labor are not yet priced.

Clean C8 ZR1s are still expensive. A 2026 ZR1 coupe in 3LZ trim was the cheapest of 15 C8 ZR1s sold on Bring a Trailer when it went for $223,000 in late January 2026, and a 2025 Launch Edition convertible brought $301,000 there in December 2025 [7]. Classic.com counted eight secondhand C8 ZR1 sales averaging $273,375, as reported by Modern Car Collector [8].

This car will never be clean. A rebuilt or salvage title typically takes 20% to 40% off a comparable clean car [9]. Applied to the low end of the clean market, that puts a properly rebuilt Goonzquad ZR1 somewhere around $135,000 to $215,000, depending on how buyers weigh a well-documented YouTube rebuild against a structural rear hit and a transmission that had teeth knocked off.

## What's next

The drivetrain is in and the rear end is hung, so the next milestone is the first start, which the brothers hope to attempt in the next video [10]. Before that the chewed body harness has to be dealt with, possibly by pulling the dashboard, and the rat-damaged seats and trim are still unpriced. The car also shares the shop with a McLaren Senna and other projects [6].
